title: Ansible flow designer document

schema_version.description: Format version of this file; always 1.

id.description: Fixed ID of the flow (ULID). Leave it out when writing by hand: Complete IDs adds it. Never change it.

key.description: Short name of the flow: lowercase letters, digits and dashes. Names the generated playbook.

version.description: Bumped once per commit when the design changes (not for layout moves). Tools bump it; do not edit by hand.

goal.description: What the flow achieves, in a sentence.

owner.description: Team or person that owns the flow.

kind.description: awx_job (one playbook), awx_workflow (approval segments) or ansible_playbook (local runs only).

template.description: Name of the AWX job or workflow template.

runtime.description: How the flow runs in AWX: a job template, or a workflow when approvals split it.

imported_from.description: Where an imported flow came from, for reference only: a one-time copy

kind.description: What the flow was imported from.

template.description: Name of the imported AWX workflow template.

id.description: ID of the imported template in AWX.

maintenance_window.description: Longest time the flow may take, e.g. 4h or 2h30m (Timing lens)

inputs.description: Inputs a run asks for. A host_list input with targets: true seeds the hosts entering the start node.

flow.description: The flow itself: identity, version, goal and the inputs a run asks for.

nodes.description: Nodes of the top level, in any order. Subflow nodes hold their own inner level under subflow.

edges.description: Wires of the top level: an output port of one node to an input port of another node on the same level. One wire per output port.

layout.description: Canvas positions of every node at every level, by node ID (or by key while written by hand). Optional: missing positions are laid out automatically.

node.description: The node the decision is about (open_on_purpose, drift_ignored).

port.description: open_on_purpose: the fail port left open on purpose.

kind.description: open_on_purpose: a fail port stays unwired on purpose (hosts stop there); drift_ignored: design and code differ on purpose; finding_accepted: a lens finding is expected.

item.description: drift_ignored: the drift item kept as it is

finding.description: finding_accepted: the lens finding kept as expected

reason.description: Why. Required in practice: the designer asks for it.

by.description: Who decided (Git user name). Tools fill it in.

items.description: One decision. kind decides which fields it needs.

decisions.description: Choices people made about the design: a fail port left open on purpose, a drift item or a lens finding kept as it is.

ulid.description: A ULID: 26 characters, digits and uppercase letters (no I, L, O, U). Written by the designer and tools; never invent one by hand.

slug.description: Lowercase letters, digits and single dashes, e.g. backup-config.

nodeRef.description: A node: its ID, or its key while the file is written by hand. 'Complete IDs' (designer quick fix, or the flow_complete_ids tool) replaces keys with IDs.

type.description: Value type. host_list is a list of inventory hosts or groups.

required.description: Inputs: a run must provide a value.

default.description: Inputs: value used when none is given.

from.description: Where the value comes from: <node_key>.<output> (an earlier node's output, on this level or around it), flow.<input> (a flow input), <subflow_key>.<input> inside that subflow (its input), or impl.register[.path] (outputs: the bound task's registered result). A subflow's outputs name an inner step's output (<step>.<output>); without from, the inner output of the same name.

targets.description: Flow inputs only: this host_list input seeds the start node's host set.

contract.description: Named inputs or outputs: name -> field.

port.description: A port name. Which ports a node has depends on its type: see the port catalog. Parallel branch ports are branch_1, branch_2, ...

node.description: The node: its ID, or its key while written by hand.

port.description: Port name: an output (from) or an input (to) of that node.

portref.description: One end of a wire: a node and one of its ports.

id.description: Fixed ID of the wire (ULID). Leave it out when writing by hand: Complete IDs adds it.

from.description: The output port the hosts leave from.

to.description: The input port they enter (usually in).

edge.description: A wire from an output port to an input port on the same level. Its hosts are the hosts that took that output.

ref.description: Fully qualified module or role name (e.g. ansible.builtin.ping, netops.baseline), or the playbook path in the repository.

collection_version.description: Collection version the binding was made against.

params.description: Module parameters or role variables. Jinja may reference inputs by name.

register.description: Variable that keeps the task result; outputs read it with from: impl.register.

impl.description: What the node runs: an Ansible module, a role or a playbook. null or absent: the node runs as a TODO stub (walking skeleton).

additionalProperties.description: Top-left corner of the node on the canvas, in pixels.

layout.description: Positions by node ID (or by key while written by hand).

id.description: Fixed ID of the node (ULID). Leave it out when writing by hand: Complete IDs adds it. Never change it.

key.description: Short name, unique on its level: lowercase letters, digits and dashes. Wires and from: references may use it.

type.description: start (one, on the top level; hosts enter), end (hosts leave; outcome success or failed), task, subflow (has an inner level), decision (true/false per host), approval (a person approves), parallel (branches), join (branches meet).

title.description: Human name shown on the canvas.

intent.description: What the node should do, in a sentence. Skeleton runs print it.

status.description: How far the node is built: draft (an idea), specified (has inputs or outputs), implemented (bound to code), tested (a passing run; set by runs only).

inputs.description: Values the node needs, usually from: an earlier node or a flow input.

outputs.description: Values the node produces for later nodes.

ports.description: Optional ports enabled beyond the type defaults (e.g. unreachable, timeout, always on a task).

impl.description: What the node runs: a module, a role or a playbook. Absent: a TODO stub.

undo.description: What reverses the node, run by Rollback for the failed hosts.

condition.description: Decision nodes: Jinja test without braces, evaluated per host; it reads the node's inputs

join_mode.description: Join nodes: per host, all = every branch delivered the host (default), any = at least one

branches.description: Parallel nodes: number of branch ports branch_1..branch_n (default 2)

handler.description: Marks a failure handler node (what kind of handling it does)

max_fail_percentage.description: Fail the whole node when more than this share of hosts fail.

serial.description: Batch size or percentage for rolling execution.

timeout.description: Task timeout, e.g. 300 or 5m. Hosts that time out leave through the timeout port.

retries.description: Retries before a host fails (module steps). Without until, a step stops retrying on its first success.

delay.description: Seconds between retries (Ansible delay, default 5). retries x delay is how long a step polls.

until.description: Poll until this holds: a Jinja test without braces, e.g. wait_ha_result.json.results | length == 2. It reads the step's registered result (impl.register, else <key with _ for ->_result) and its inputs. Module steps only; retries sets the attempts.

inventory_target.description: Run the node's work on this host pattern instead of the arriving hosts (they leave together afterwards).

tags.description: Extra Ansible tags for the generated play.

layout.description: Old place for inner positions: read, never written (positions live in the top-level layout).

in.description: The inner node that receives the hosts entering the subflow.

additionalProperties.description: Inner outputs leaving through this port.

outputs.description: Exits: a parent port name -> the inner outputs that leave through it.

boundary.description: How hosts enter and leave the subflow.

subflow.description: Subflow nodes: the inner level and how hosts enter and leave it.

node.description: A step of the flow. Its type decides its ports; its status says how far it is built.
The inner node: its ID, or its key while written by hand.

reason.description: Why hosts leave the subflow here (shown on the exit wire)

exitref.description: An inner output that leaves the subflow.

description: An Ansible flow: a graph of typed nodes wired port to port. Hosts travel along the wires; every control port carries the hosts that took it. The designer edits this file; tools and AI assistants may write it too.
